blk_introduction.text: Your plane lands in Vilnius, the capital of Lithuania. You are tired, but you are happy too.
You have five questions: how to pay, how to get to the city, what to see, how to check in and what to eat. In this simulation, you take each step in time order.
You learn real prices and real times. You also practise simple English for each step.

blk_part_1_part_1_you_land_at_vilnius_ai.text: You land at Vilnius International Airport. This airport is the main airport for Vilnius. Many airlines fly here. You walk with the other people to passport control. You wait in a line. An officer looks at your passport. Then you take your bag.

Next, you think about money. Prices in Vilnius are in euros (€). For example, a bus ticket from the airport to the city centre costs €1. You buy this bus ticket from the driver. So it is good to have your payment ready before you get on the bus.
Your phone is important too. You need maps and the Bolt app. So you look for a SIM card. You do not know the price yet. Ask at the shop before you buy.

blk_part_2_part_2_you_choose_a_ride_to_t.text: You have three good ways to get to the city. Each way has a different time and price.

The first way is the train. The train goes from the airport to the central railway station. The trip is 4.3 km long. It takes about 7 or 8 minutes. A ticket costs €0.45, and you can buy it online. This train is fast and cheap. But it runs only 16 times a day. So check the next train time first.

The second way is the bus. The bus takes about 15 minutes to the city centre. Several buses go to the city centre and the Old Town. You can buy a €1 ticket from the driver. City tickets cost €1 for 30 minutes or €1.25 for 60 minutes.

The third way is a taxi or a ride app. A taxi from the airport to Cathedral Square in the Old Town costs about €10. It takes about 15 minutes. You find taxis at the arrivals area. Bolt is a big ride company in Vilnius. Bolt and Uber work 24 hours a day, every day. Open the app and check the price before you say yes.
How can I get to the Old Town?
Where can I buy a ticket?

blk_part_3_part_3_your_first_look_at_the.text: You arrive in the city. You walk into Vilnius Old Town. The Old Town is very old. Many of its streets and buildings come from the medieval period, about 500 to 1,000 years ago. It is one of the largest old towns in Northern Europe. So you see many small streets and many old buildings.
One is Cathedral Square. The other is Town Hall Square. You also see the buildings of Vilnius University. They are a famous part of the Old Town.

Then you see the Gate of Dawn. This is an important old gate. People built it between 1503 and 1514. It was part of the city wall. Later, people took down most of the city walls. But they kept this gate. It has a famous picture of the Virgin Mary. Many people come here to pray. The church services are in Lithuanian and Polish.

blk_part_4_part_4_you_check_in_and_ask_f.text: You find your hotel. You go to the front desk.  You show your passport. The staff member gives you a key card. Now you have a room.

You are new in Vilnius, so ask for help. The front desk is a good place for questions. Ask for the Wi-Fi password. Ask for a map. Ask for the way to Cathedral Square or Town Hall Square. These are big squares in the Old Town, so they are easy places to meet people or start a walk.
You can ask about food too. Hotel staff know the area.
Can you show me on the map?

blk_part_5_part_5_your_first_lithuanian_.text: You go to a restaurant near your hotel. You look at the menu.
The cook boils them. They come with a sour cream sauce and small bits of bacon or pork rind. This is a warm, heavy meal. It is good after a long trip.

The second dish is šaltibarščiai. This is a cold soup, and it is bright pink. It has boiled and cooled beetroot, cucumber, green onion, dill and other herbs. The beetroot gives it the pink colour. People in Vilnius love this soup. Since 2023, Vilnius has a festival for this soup every year.
The menu shows the prices in euros. Read the price before you order.
I would like the cepelinai, please.
Can I have the bill, please?

blk_scene_1_at_the_airport_information_d.text: You have your bag, and you are at the arrivals area of Vilnius Airport. Your hotel is in the Old Town. You see an information desk.
Your goal is to choose a ride to the Old Town and learn the time, the price and where to buy a ticket.

blk_scene_2_at_the_hotel_front_desk.text: You walk through the Old Town and arrive at your hotel. You feel tired but happy.
Your goal is to check in, get help with your phone and ask about food and the way to Town Hall Square.

blk_scene_3_dinner_at_a_lithuanian_resta.text: You find the restaurant near your hotel. It is warm and busy inside. A server named Eglė gives you a menu.
Your goal is to ask about the dishes, order your meal and pay.

blk_speaking_task.text: Work with a partner. Tell the story of your first day in Vilnius. Use "I" and the present tense. Start at the airport and end at dinner. Choose the train, the bus or a taxi, and say the time and the price. Say one thing about the Old Town or the Gate of Dawn. Then order one dish. Your partner asks two questions, for example "Why do you choose the bus?" and "What is in the soup?" Then change roles.
